notes:
I don't have any notes on Psalm 147 for you yet, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

I tried to open six pages: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Augustine's sermon on this psalm at New Advent, and the NET Bible notes. The first attempt failed because of a mistake in how I handled the results. I then hit the limit on web lookups for this turn before I could try again, and the other tools I have can't go online. So I read nothing from any of the sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say, with a URL for each point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Any notes I wrote now would break those rules, so I haven't written any.

**What I'll do when you ask again (for example, by replying "continue"):**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word; Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and other older works on Bible Hub and StudyLight; Precept Austin. I'll also try Spurgeon's commentary on the Psalms if it's available on one of the allowed sites.
2. **Protestant differences:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), and Reformed, Baptist, Lutheran and Pentecostal sites. I'll include a verse only where a real difference turns up. Verses 19–20, about God giving His word to Israel alone, are the likeliest place for that.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship. Augustine's sermon on New Advent for the Catholic reading; in the older Latin numbering, Psalm 147 is split across two psalms, 146 and 147. Orthodox readings from oca.org. I'll cover popular modern teaching (such as prosperity) only if the allowed sites actually discuss it in connection with this psalm.

The notes will be written verse by verse ("v. 4: …"), in my own words, with a URL after each point. I'll leave out anything I can't find.
